html: Luis Ramiro Barragán Morfín is born on 9 March in Guadalajara, Jalisco, into a family of landowners. Childhood summers at the family ranch near Mazamitla leave a lasting memory of adobe walls, water channels and village colour.
Graduates as a civil engineer from the Escuela Libre de Ingenieros in Guadalajara. He never takes a formal degree in architecture.
Travels through France and Spain. The gardens of Ferdinand Bac and the Alhambra in Granada shape his understanding of the garden as an enclosed, private world.
Builds his first houses and gardens in Guadalajara, among them Casa González Luna and Casa Cristo, and the Parque de la Revolución.
Second journey: New York, then Paris, where he attends lectures by Le Corbusier and meets Ferdinand Bac in person.
Settles in Mexico City and works for several years as a developer and architect of functionalist apartment buildings.
Withdraws from commercial practice. Buys land in Tacubaya and begins a series of experimental private gardens.
Plans Jardines del Pedregal on the lava fields south of the city, with gardens and show houses that establish his mature language of walls, water and landscape.
Completes his own house and studio in Tacubaya, which he continues to alter for the rest of his life.
Completes the chapel and convent for the Capuchinas Sacramentarias in Tlalpan, and Casa Gálvez in San Ángel.
With Mathias Goeritz, builds the five coloured towers of Ciudad Satélite.
Completes Cuadra San Cristóbal for the Egerström family at Los Clubes, with Andrés Casillas.
A retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, with a monograph by Emilio Ambasz, brings his work to an international audience.
Completes Casa Gilardi in San Miguel Chapultepec, with its yellow corridor and indoor pool.

On 31 October he signs the elevation drawings for a house in Bosques de las Lomas for his friend Barbara Meyer, inscribed para Baby Meyer de Garate, con todo cariño. It is his last residential project.
Receives the Pritzker Architecture Prize. In his acceptance speech he speaks of serenity, silence, solitude and the garden.
The Faro del Comercio in Monterrey, his last built work.
Dies on 22 November at his house in Tacubaya.
Casa Luis Barragán is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
